    On Call
    • Film

    Thursday, September 10, 2026
    7 PM
    On Call
    Alice Diop,
    France,
    2016,
    (96 mins)
    One small medical office holds an eternity of stories in Alice Diop’s fly-on-the-wall observational documentary that bears witness to a doctor’s steady stream of patients—immigrants, refugees, and undocumented immigrants—as they reveal their physical and mental suffering. “To see On Call is a therapy against the reflexes of exclusion” (Olivier Barlet, Black Camera).

    Senegalese Meet Sene-Gallic
    • Film
    • Free
    • In-Person
    Friday, September 18, 2026
    7 PM
    Senegalese Meet Sene-Gallic
    Alice Diop,
    France, Senegal,
    2007,
    (77 mins)

    Free admission. Tickets available at the admissions desk at 6 PM.

    Two shorts that mark the beginning and the current state of Alice Diop’s visionary filmmaking: Les Sénégalaises et la Sénégauloise finds her musing on migration, exile, and fate in her mother’s former home in Senegal, while Fragments for Venus (2025) follows one woman’s visit to the Louvre to see Black lives in art, and another’s visit to Bed-Stuy to witness the art of Black life.

    Free admission. Tickets available at the admissions desk at 6 PM.

    • Maya Sidhu
      Introduction
      Maya Sidhu is a Lecturer in the Department of French at UC Berkeley. She is currently writing a book on the films of Alice Diop.

      The opening shot of this striking environmental tale captures a tree as tall as a fifteen-story building floating on a barge across the vast Black Sea. Its destination lies in a garden countless miles away, privately owned by a wealthy and anonymous man.
      In Conversation
      • Salomé Jashi

        Elene Naveriani is the director of Blackbird Blackbird Blackberry and Wet Sand.

      Georgian Cinema Now Symposium—Activism in Authoritarian Times: The Republic of Georgia as a Case Study

      Free Admission

      Copresented by the Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive and the Institute of Slavic, East European, and Eurasian Studies at UC Berkeley

      Promotional partner: Center for Russian, East European, and Eurasian Studies at Stanford University

      This symposium is timed with the launch of BAMPFA’s series Georgian Cinema Now. Presentations by visiting Georgian artists and experts will offer greater context and insights into the current situation for independent filmmakers and journalists working in Georgia today.

      Free and open to the public. Tickets available at the admissions desk beginning at 11 AM.

      English Teacher and Bakhmaro 2050

      These two creative documentaries that ruminate on issues facing Georgian society are both set far from city life.       Self-Portrait Along the Borderline
      Anna Dziapshipa,
      Georgia,
      2023,
      (79 mins)
      Anna Dziapshipa was born of the union between an Abkhazian man and a Georgian woman. In Self-Portrait Along the Borderline, she skillfully weaves together unique archives and fragments to offer a personal and political biography of Georgia–Abkhazia relations. With Dziapshipa’s shorts Contemplation and Dear Dirty Tbilisi.
